adversarial_probes.method: 5 independent probes authored as a temporary vitest spec (ci/checks/db/_probe_t0062_adversarial.test.ts) using the REAL pgOutboxStore/pgJobStore/runOutboxOnce against the live isolated pool under dedicated probe tenants; all 5 PASS; file DELETED after run, working tree clean (git status porcelain empty).
adversarial_probes.A_concurrent_idempotency_race: PASS — 8x Promise.all enqueue(topic,vars,0,sameKey) on a real choros_app pool (session GUC=TENANT) → DB COUNT=1, all 8 callers returned the same jobId (set size 1). ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING + SELECT-back is race-safe (each enqueue auto-commit; loser observes committed row).
adversarial_probes.B_outbox_atomicity_rollback: PASS — domain job INSERT + outbox.enqueueInTx(client,...) on one PoolClient in one BEGIN, then ROLLBACK → 0 domain rows AND 0 outbox rows. enqueueInTx opens no tx of its own; atomicity enforced by the API shape (requires caller's PoolClient).
adversarial_probes.C_dispatcher_phase2_handler_throws: PASS — deliver() throws → runOutboxOnce catches → markRetry: row state=pending, attempts=1, available_at=now+backoff (future), last_error~/boom/, exactly 1 row (not duplicated), result {dispatched:0,failed:1,dead:0}. Not lost, not double-claimed.
adversarial_probes.D_dead_exhaustion: PASS — row at attempts=2, maxAttempts=3, deliver fails → state=dead, attempts=3, r1.dead=1, getOutboxHealth.deadCount grew; second runOutboxOnce returned {0,0,0} (dead row NOT re-claimed by claimBatch state='pending' filter).
adversarial_probes.E_security_definer_aggregate: PASS — choros_app WITHOUT GUC: outbox_pending_buckets() returns exactly columns [pending_count, tenant_id] (no payload/id/aggregate_*); a seeded row with payload {secret:'leak-me'} did NOT leak. Contrast: raw SELECT count(*) FROM choros.outbox without GUC = 0 rows (fail-closed, FORCE RLS default-DENY).

integration_honesty_D056.real_substrate: All AC/probe assertions ran against a real Postgres 16 (RLS, FORCE RLS, SECURITY DEFINER, FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, partial index, EXPLAIN) — no mocks for the DB layer. The dispatcher unit tests use a fake store by design (pure-orchestration class), but every DB invariant they orchestrate is independently covered by live integration tests + probes.
integration_honesty_D056.no_file_parallelism_justified: Global package.json fitness:db --no-file-parallelism is a shared-PG-race guard (D-056); did not mask defects — the concurrency-sensitive checks (AC-12 SKIP LOCKED, PROBE_A 8-way race) assert concurrency INSIDE a single file and pass; CI time unaffected (6.18s).
integration_honesty_D056.fresh_db_reproduction: Gate reproduced the review's green run on a brand-new isolated volume (migrate-from-zero x2 then fitness:db), not a warm/pre-seeded DB — confirms the migrations are self-sufficient and idempotent end-to-end.

anti_false_fail_discipline.probe_B_pg_deprecation_warning: PROBE_B emitted a pg DeprecationWarning ('client.query() while already executing') from the test's connect-hook (void c.query SET GUC) racing the explicit BEGIN — a harness artifact in MY probe scaffolding, NOT product code; the rollback assertions still held. Classified tooling-nuance, not a product defect.
anti_false_fail_discipline.review_nit_R1_markRetry_noop: markRetry returns 'pending'|'dead'|'noop'; 'noop' is an ADDITIVE, correct extension over ADR §4.2's 'pending'|'dead' signature — it honestly handles the concurrent-claim race (UPDATE WHERE state='dispatching' → 0 rows). PROBE_C/D exercised the live paths and confirmed monotonic-forward transitions only. Verdict: documentation lag, not a defect (consistent with reviewer R-1).
